title: Phased migration from stateful-session endpoints to stateless-session-proxy-adapter
creator: Aisha Patel
description: This PRD describes the phased deprecation of stateful session endpoints (historically used for long-running conversations and server-side session storage) and the introduction of a stateless session proxy adapter. The goal is to remove server-side session affinity and replace it with a header- and token-based stateless model plus an opt-in proxy adapter for legacy clients who cannot upgrade before enforcement windows.
background: Several internal scalability and SLO initiatives require us to eliminate per-session server affinity (large KV caches and sticky routing increase tail latency and capacity fragmentation). A stateless model using client-provided session tokens and compact server-side KV only for hot prefixes reduces complexity and enables better autoscaling and caching. Historically this work has been requested by infra and runtime teams (ENG-40212, ENG-41988) and aligns with the Optimize roadmap to reduce per-token cost.
goals: Provide a clear migration path and adapter for clients using stateful session endpoints
Minimize customer disruption during phased deprecation
Reduce session-related tail latency by 40% in the long tail
Enable autoscaling improvements that reduce idle GPU hours by 15% on Dedicated
non_goals: Replace customer-managed session stores that live outside Redwood (out of scope)
Re-architecting client SDKs beyond an adapter (full client rewrites are the customer's responsibility)
migration_strategy: Three-phase approach: 1) Announcement & documentation (60 days) with SDK adapter preview; 2) Opt-in compatibility window with proxy adapter and telemetry gates; 3) Enforcement window where legacy endpoints return 410 with migration tips and automatic adapter block for customers who opted-in but did not migrate.
milestones: 2026-04-01: Public deprecation notice and migration docs published
2026-05-15: SDK adapter v0.1 released (npm/pypi) + opt-in compatibility flag available in Console
2026-07-01: Telemetry gating & migration dashboard visible in Console (per-customer progress)
2026-09-01: Enforcement begins — legacy stateful endpoints return 410 for non-adapter traffic
2026-12-01: Final data-removal window and hard shutdown of stateful session backend
migration_steps: Publish migration guide with code samples for exchange of session-state to stateless tokens
Release SDK adapter that translates legacy session calls into stateless requests (best-effort, rate-limited)
Expose Console migration dashboard showing percent of requests using adapter vs native stateless flow
Implement server-side telemetry gating to require adapter header or new session token after opt-in
Coordinate with Support for targeted outreach to high-usage customers during compatibility window
Blackout testing and gradual rollout with canary customers before enforcement
acceptance_criteria: Migration docs published and linked from Console + in-product migration banner
SDK adapter published on npm/pypi with README and example conversions
Migration dashboard shows per-API-key migration progress and per-customer error trends
Less than 3% increase in 5xx rates during canary rollouts; if exceeded, rollback gates present
95% of active API keys either migrate to stateless tokens or enable adapter before 2026-09-01 (measured by dashboard)
Latency SLOs for conversation workloads improve in long-tail percentiles by at least 20% in pilot clusters
Security review completed and KMS integration validated for token exchange flows
observability_and_telemetry: Add dimensions for: original endpoint (legacy vs stateless), adapter-used (true/false), customer api_key, migration-phase, error-class. Create dashboard alarms for >0.5% adapter-error-rate by customer and global 5xx spikes post-enforcement.
rollback_plan: If enforcement causes systemic customer outages or SLO regressions, immediately re-enable legacy routing for impacted customers and extend opt-in window. Rollback criteria: sustained 5xx increase >1% for 30m or critical customer SLA impact. Retro report to execs within 48h.
communication_plan: Week 0 (2026-04-01): Public deprecation email to all billing contacts + in-product banner
Ongoing: Weekly migration digest with top 50 customers and migration blockers
Two weeks before enforcement: targeted outreach and scheduled migration sessions for high-use customers
Post-enforcement: status page updates and post-mortem for any incidents
customer_support_requirements: Support runbook with playback scripts, steps to enable adapter, diagnostics to collect (logs, request IDs), escalation path to Platform Eng and PM. Pre-authorized emergency migrations for enterprise customers with dedicated SLAs.
risks_mitigations: Risk: Customers unable to upgrade before enforcement — Mitigation: robust SDK adapter + extended compatibility windows for top 20 customers
Risk: Adapter adds latency — Mitigation: adapter is rate-limited and runs in edge cache with metrics; measure percentiles and iterate
Risk: Security exposure during token exchange — Mitigation: KMS-backed token signing, short TTLs, mandatory rotation policy
notes: Owner: PM (Aisha) + ENG tech lead (Rana Bose, ENG-40212)
